title: Adaptive translucency and per-brand tint mapping for dense console surfaces (dark mode)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: As we expand brand theming and compact density modes, certain dense surfaces (tables, sparklines, compact controls) lose visual hierarchy in dark mode. Existing token fallbacks produce muddy charts, low-contrast table rows, and buttons whose depress/hover states clash with brand tints. Goal: define a small set of perceptually-consistent translucency and tint tokens plus component override rules that preserve contrast, maintain brand presence, and work reliably at compact densities and varied alpha/backdrop conditions.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a minimal token set for translucency and tint anchoring (3 tokens) and document algorithm for scaling tints across brand variants
Charts and table rows use new tokens with no automated contrast regressions vs current baseline (WCAG AA for text on primary table surfaces)
Figma components updated with examples for 3 brand tints and compact densities; design review signoff obtained
Design tokens exported and reviewed with runtime team; PR with token JSON + spec merged
QA checklist for visual diffs on flagship pages created and linked
design_notes: Strategy: keep token count small to reduce runtime permutations. New tokens live alongside existing semantic surfaces rather than replace them.
Perceptual approach: use LAB-based tint scaling with fixed luminance anchors rather than linear alpha stacking to avoid hue shifts on dark backdrops.
Tokens proposed: surface.glass (backdrop-aware translucency), surface.tint-anchor (brand-neutral anchor used for blending), brand.tint-lean (subtle brand wash for chrome and legends).

Component overrides: charts should prefer stroke: brand.tint-lean at 60% contrast to surface.elev-1; table zebra stripes use surface.glass with 6–8% luminance delta from surface.base in compact density; buttons keep solid brand fills for primary but use brand.tint-lean on secondary fills to avoid saturation in dark mode.
Density considerations: compact spacing reduces visible separation; increase elevation/contrast tokens slightly for compact mode only (compact.surface-elev-1).
Accessibility: ensure body text on any new surface meets AA; interactive hit states must maintain 3:1 contrast with adjacent background where text is not present.
decisions: Adopt three new tokens instead of a large token matrix to limit combinatorial explosion: surface.glass, surface.tint-anchor, brand.tint-lean.
Use LAB perceptual mixing for tint blending in the token specification and provide a reference implementation for engineers.
Introduce a compact mode modifier tokenset (compact.surface-elev-*) instead of altering global tokens to keep normal & compact predictable.
Charts and legends will use tint tokens for strokes/area fills; gradients must preserve stroke contrast at narrow widths.
open_questions: Should backdrop blur be exposed as a token or only used in Figma prototypes? (pros/cons: runtime cost vs design fidelity)
Do we need per-brand lightness clamps to avoid brand tints that are too saturated on extreme dark backgrounds?
Can the engineering team provide a small JS utility that returns blended RGB from LAB inputs to standardize blending?
implementation_notes: Provide exact LAB anchors in the spec so runtime can implement deterministic blending: surface.tint-anchor L=10, a=0, b=0; brand.tint-lean maps to brand primary at 12% perceptual lightness lift; surface.glass is defined as 0.06 luminance delta above surface.base in dark mode.
Fallback behavior: if runtime cannot perform perceptual blending, fallback to 8% alpha overlay of brand color on surface.base (documented as less preferred).
Include unit visual tests: small multiples for 3 brands x 2 densities x 4 components (table, chart legend, compact button, tooltip).
